blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: The inventory team's ReorderPolicy takes a WarehouseClient in its constructor and calls its place(...) method. WarehouseClient is an interface declared in the warehouse team's jar. The inventory team compiles ReorderPolicy in a module of its own, with only its own sources and the JDK. What happens?

options.text: It fails to compile, since javac needs a class that implements WarehouseClient, and the module has no such class
options.says: javac needs the types the policy names, not an implementation; with the interface in the policy's own package it compiles alone

options.text: It fails to compile, since javac needs the declaration of WarehouseClient, and the module has no such declaration
options.says: an interface the detail publishes is still a type in the detail's jar; the policy can't compile without it

options.text: It compiles, since javac needs WarehouseClient's declaration only for a class that implements it, and the module has no such class
options.says: injecting an interface is not inversion when the interface lives in the detail's jar; javac still needs that jar

options.text: It compiles, since javac needs the warehouse jar only for a call to new, and the module has no such call
options.says: every type a source file names must be on the compile path, interfaces included, not only where new is called

origin.section: The Interface Belongs to the Policy, So the Policy Compiles Without the Mail Code

questions.stem: ShippingQuoter has a no-argument constructor, and its quote() method starts by getting a RateTable with Services.get(RateTable.class), from a global registry that main fills in before serving requests. A release deletes the line in main that registers the RateTable. When does the mistake show?

options.text: It fails at start-up, since Services.get(RateTable.class) runs when main builds ShippingQuoter
options.says: the constructor takes nothing and looks nothing up; the lookup is in quote()

options.text: It fails at start-up, since main's filling of the registry checks for a RateTable
options.says: filling the registry checks nothing; the missing entry is found only when something asks for it

options.text: It fails at the first quote() call, since Services.get(RateTable.class) runs when quote() runs
options.says: the lookup runs when quote() runs; the service compiles, starts and serves anything that doesn't quote

options.text: It fails at the first quote() call, since main's filling of the registry is deferred until quote() runs
options.says: main fills the registry at start-up; get() only reads it

origin.section: A Constructor Parameter Turns a Forgotten Dependency Into a Compile Error

questions.stem: Two tests check SeatBooking. One uses a Mockito mock SeatStore, stubs isFree and reserve, and ends with verify(store).isFree("14F") and verify(store).reserve("14F"). The other uses a hand-written fake SeatStore and asserts which bookings succeed. SeatStore also has reserveIfFree(seat), which returns false when the seat is taken. A colleague changes SeatBooking to call only reserveIfFree, so two bookings can't both see the seat free; it accepts and refuses the same bookings as before. What happens to the two tests?

options.text: Both tests pass, since verify checks that each named method had a stubbed answer, and the fake answers reserveIfFree from the seats it has reserved so far
options.says: verify checks that each named call was made; isFree no longer is

options.text: Both tests fail, since verify checks that each named method was called, and the fake answers reserveIfFree from a table of answers the test filled in
options.says: a fake is a working implementation of the whole interface; it needs no per-test answers, and the bookings are the same

options.text: The mock test passes and the fake test fails, since verify checks that each named method had a stubbed answer, and the fake answers reserveIfFree from a table of answers the test filled in
options.says: verify checks calls, and a fake answers from its own state

options.text: The mock test fails and the fake test passes, since verify checks that each named method was called, and the fake answers reserveIfFree from the seats it has reserved so far
options.says: the mock test pinned the calls, which changed; the fake test checks the decisions, which didn't

origin.section: A Fake Checks the Outcome; a Mock Checks the Calls

questions.stem: The tax rules for Germany move into a new jar, tax-de.jar. Its listing shows META-INF/MANIFEST.MF and tax/de/GermanRules.class, a public class with a public no-argument constructor that implements TaxRules. With tax-de.jar on the class path, the application calls ServiceLoader.load(TaxRules.class).findFirst(). What does it get?

options.text: A GermanRules instance, since the listed public class with a public no-argument constructor is enough for the loader
options.says: those are needed, but on the class path a provider without the services file is not found

options.text: A GermanRules instance, since the loader scans the listed classes once no META-INF/services file names a provider
options.says: ServiceLoader doesn't scan classes; it reads the services file

options.text: An empty Optional, since the loader learns provider names only from a META-INF/services file, and the listing has none
options.says: ServiceLoader reads META-INF/services/<interface name>; a jar without it contributes no provider

options.text: An empty Optional, since the loader learns provider names only from META-INF/MANIFEST.MF, and the listed one names none
options.says: the manifest plays no part; the provider-configuration file under META-INF/services does

origin.section: ServiceLoader Picks the Implementation From the Class Path

concepts: A test with a fake checks the outcome and survives a refactor that changes the calls; a mock test that verifies calls fails it although no decision changed.
Injecting an interface that the detail's jar declares is injection without inversion: the policy still can't compile without that jar; the interface belongs in the policy's package, in its terms.
ServiceLoader finds class-path providers only through META-INF/services/<interface name>; a provider class on the class path without that file is not found.
